The 90-day cohort is the cleaner cut: 19 tracked homes have passed three months on market, 15 of them are still active and 4 reached contract — and that 4 is a lower bound, because a home loses its cumulative-days figure once it closes. 6 of the 26 pendings had cut price before finding a buyer. read.headline: 71 active listings, but only 18 of them sit in a 9/10 catchment — and at 6.66% the math still favours renting until roughly year 15.
points: Inventory is wide but shallow where it counts. Of 71 active 4BD homes under $2M, just 18 are zoned to one of the four target elementaries: Newport Heights 10, Somerset 6, Audubon 1, Woodridge 1. The other 53 come from the broad Redmond 98052 and Bellevue 98008 sweeps, where the elementary assignment still has to be confirmed address by address. Newport Heights is the only strong-school catchment offering real choice under $1.5M — five of its ten listings qualify, starting at $1,280,000. Somerset's six all open at $1,750,000 or above, and Audubon remains a one-home market.

Sellers are still the ones moving. The Aug 1 refresh logged 8 new listings against 5 price cuts totalling $292,500 and 6 homes leaving the market. Both core ZIP medians are negative year-over-year — Redmond 98052 at $1,302,113 (−3.9%) and Bellevue 98008 at $1,469,064 (−5.2%) — so the softness is showing up in the comparables, not just in individual negotiations. 29 of the 71 listings are now under $1.5M.

Financing is the headwind. The 30-yr fixed rose to 6.66% (Freddie Mac, Jul 30) from 6.58% the week before. On a $1.5M purchase at 20% down that is about $10,174/mo to own — $7,712 of it mortgage principal and interest, the rest tax, insurance and maintenance — against $4,772/mo for a comparable 4BD rental. Over a 7-year horizon at 3% appreciation, renting comes out roughly $179,000 cheaper, and buying does not pull ahead until around year 15.

A cheaper entry moves the breakeven far more than the rate does. Run the same model on the least expensive strong-school listing ($1,280,000, Newport Heights) and the monthly cost to own falls to about $8,704, the 7-year gap narrows to roughly $89,000, and breakeven arrives near year 11 — four years sooner. Reference home C ($1,548,900, unchanged this refresh) goes the other way: more house and nearly an acre, but about $10,501/mo, a Lake Hills 5/10 zone, and a wider 7-year gap of roughly $200,000 for the same year-15 breakeven.

What this implies. At 6.66% a purchase only clears the rent comparison on a long stay, so the school catchment — not the cost math — is what would justify buying now. Only 6 of the 71 listings are both under $1.5M and inside a 9/10 zone, and five of those are Newport Heights. That narrow band, from $1,280,000 up, is where the shortest breakeven and the strongest school overlap.
